glossary.lesion: Any area of damage or abnormal tissue, such as a tumour, infarct or patch of inflammation.
glossary.visual pathway: The chain of nerves and brain areas carrying signals from the retina to the visual cortex.
glossary.retina: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye that turns light into nerve signals.
glossary.nasal retina: The half of the retina nearest the nose; it sees the outer (temporal) half of the visual field.
glossary.temporal visual field: The outer half of what each eye sees, towards the side of the head.
glossary.temporal lobe: The part of the brain at the side, under the temple, involved in hearing and memory.
glossary.parietal lobe: The upper middle part of the brain, processing sensation and spatial awareness.
glossary.occipital lobe: The back part of the brain, containing the primary visual cortex.
glossary.occipital pole: The very back tip of the occipital lobe, where central (macular) vision is processed.
glossary.contralateral: On the opposite side of the body to the lesion.
glossary.ipsilateral: On the same side of the body as the lesion.
glossary.pie in the sky: Nickname for a superior quadrantanopia from a temporal lobe lesion.
glossary.pie on the floor: Nickname for an inferior quadrantanopia from a parietal lobe lesion.
glossary.chiasmal compression: Pressure on the optic chiasm, usually from a mass in or above the pituitary fossa.
glossary.multiple sclerosis: An autoimmune disease where the immune system strips myelin from nerves in the brain and spinal cord.
glossary.posterior cerebral artery: The artery supplying the occipital lobe; its blockage is the classic cause of occipital infarcts.
glossary.middle cerebral artery: The main artery to the side of each cerebral hemisphere; its branches also reach the occipital pole.
glossary.collaterals: Alternative blood vessels that can supply an area when its main artery is blocked.
glossary.dual blood supply: Fed by two separate arteries, so the tissue can survive if one is blocked.
glossary.infarct: An area of tissue that has died because its blood supply was cut off.
glossary.MRI: Magnetic resonance imaging: a scan using magnets and radio waves, best for showing soft tissue like brain.
glossary.gold standard: The most accurate, definitive test or treatment against which others are judged.
glossary.pre-chiasm: In front of the optic chiasm, so only one eye's fibres are affected.
glossary.pituitary tumour: A growth of the pituitary gland, which sits just below the optic chiasm.
glossary.visual cortex: The area of the occipital lobe that receives and interprets signals from the eyes.
glossary.NICE: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence: the body writing national clinical guidelines in England.
